body:
Why was ANRF established?

Scientific research in India is undertaken by universities, colleges, government laboratories, specialised institutes and private organisations. Research capacity, however, is not distributed equally across these institutions. Some have advanced facilities and established funding systems, while others are developing their research capabilities.

The Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) was established to provide high-level strategic direction and support for research, innovation and entrepreneurship across disciplines. It is a national institution concerned with the wider research system rather than the management of one particular laboratory or scientific field.

Statutory foundation and commencement

Parliament enacted the Anusandhan National Research Foundation Act, 2023, numbered Act 25 of 2023. It received assent on 12 August 2023. The Act came into force on 5 February 2024, following the notified commencement date.

ANRF is therefore established under legislation. This is different from an initiative appearing only in the draft STIP 2020.

Policy versus law: The 2020 STIP document contained proposed policy measures. The ANRF Act 2023 is legislation creating an institution and defining its objectives, governance and funding framework.

Fields and functions covered

The Act gives ANRF a broad mandate covering natural and mathematical sciences, engineering and technology, environmental and earth sciences, health, agriculture and scientific or technological interfaces with humanities and social sciences.

Important functions include:

  • Preparing short-, medium- and long-term research-development roadmaps.
  • Supporting research projects, fellowships and research facilities.
  • Providing competitive, peer-reviewed research grants to eligible applicants.
  • Strengthening research in universities and colleges where research capacity is still developing.
  • Promoting cooperation among universities, laboratories, industries and governments.
  • Supporting the conversion of research results into useful technologies.
  • Collecting and analysing information about research expenditure and outcomes.

Peer review means that a research proposal is examined by appropriately qualified experts. In a competitive grant system, funding decisions consider the quality and suitability of proposals rather than distributing an identical amount to every institution.

Governing Board and Executive Council

The Act establishes a Governing Board to provide high-level strategic direction and an Executive Council to implement the Act and administer the Foundation's work.

  • President of the Governing Board: Prime Minister of India, ex officio.
  • Vice-Presidents of the Governing Board: Union Minister of Science and Technology and Union Minister of Education, ex officio.
  • Member-Secretary of the Governing Board: Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, ex officio.
  • Chairperson of the Executive Council: Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, ex officio.

The term ex officio means that a person serves on the body by virtue of holding another specified office.

Funding and relationship with SERB

The Act permits ANRF to receive government funding and contributions from other permitted sources, including public-sector enterprises, private organisations and philanthropic bodies. Its statutory funds include the ANRF Fund, an Innovation Fund, a Science and Engineering Research Fund and provision for special-purpose funds.

Section 27 repealed the Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2008, and provided for the dissolution of the earlier Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB), while protecting specified existing rights, obligations and proceedings. The new framework includes arrangements for continuing relevant earlier research programmes.

ANRF does not replace specialised institutions such as ISRO, DRDO, ICMR or ICAR. Those organisations retain their sectoral research mandates. ANRF supports and coordinates the wider research environment.

Prelims focus

  • ANRF Act: 2023, Act 25 of 2023.
  • Presidential assent: 12 August 2023.
  • Commencement: 5 February 2024.
  • Governing Board President: Prime Minister, ex officio.
  • Executive Council Chairperson: Principal Scientific Adviser, ex officio.
  • Section 27 repealed the SERB Act, 2008.
  • Trap: ANRF is a statutory research foundation, not another name for the draft STIP 2020.

[Government of India, Anusandhan National Research Foundation Act, 2023, Act 25 of 2023, sections 1, 3–7, 13 and 27, including commencement notification dated 5 February 2024; Anusandhan National Research Foundation, About ANRF, sections Strategic Goals and Structure and Governance; sources consulted 2 November 2026.]

pictures.caption: ANRF separates strategic direction from the administration of research support.

body:
Why does India have different scientific institutions?

A country's research system cannot be managed by a single laboratory. Fundamental discoveries, industrial technologies, scientific measurements, biotechnology and education require different expertise. India therefore has departments that coordinate science, research councils that operate laboratory networks and institutions specialising in particular branches of knowledge.

The essential distinction is between policy and coordination, research and development, scientific measurement and education and training. One organisation may perform more than one of these functions.

Department of Science and Technology

The Department of Science and Technology (DST) was established in May 1971. It functions within the Union Ministry of Science and Technology. Its broad responsibilities include promoting scientific research, developing scientific capabilities, supporting institutions and coordinating suitable science and technology activities.

DST is an administrative department. It should not be confused with a specialised research laboratory. For example, a department may support scientific infrastructure while individual institutes perform the experiments and investigations.

CSIR and industrial research

The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) was established in 1942. It is a national network of research laboratories under the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research, Ministry of Science and Technology.

CSIR's work connects scientific knowledge with problems faced by industry and society. Its laboratories study fields such as materials, chemicals, industrial processes, scientific instruments and environmental technologies. Individual CSIR laboratories have distinct specialisations.

CSIR-National Physical Laboratory

CSIR-National Physical Laboratory (CSIR-NPL), New Delhi is India's national metrology institution. Metrology is the science of measurement. Reliable measurement standards allow measurements made in different laboratories, industries and locations to be compared accurately.

For example, industries and testing laboratories need dependable standards for quantities such as mass, length, temperature and electrical measurements. This is different from scientific research into the physical nature of those quantities.

CSIR-Central Salt and Marine Chemicals Research Institute

CSIR-Central Salt and Marine Chemicals Research Institute (CSIR-CSMCRI) is located at Bhavnagar, Gujarat. Its predecessor institute was inaugurated on 10 April 1954. It works on salt, marine resources and related chemical technologies.

Bhavnagar is therefore an important Gujarat example of a national scientific institution. The institute's location in Gujarat does not make CSIR a state-government research council.

Basic-science institutes and scientific education

InstitutionLocationPrincipal role
Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR)MumbaiFundamental scientific research and advanced training.
Indian Institute of Science (IISc)BengaluruHigher education and research across science and engineering.
Indian Institutes of Science Education and Research (IISERs)Multiple locationsIntegrated scientific education and research.
CSIR-NPLNew DelhiNational measurement standards and metrology.
CSIR-CSMCRIBhavnagarSalt and marine-chemical research.

TIFR was established in 1945 through the initiative of Homi J. Bhabha. It is associated with the Department of Atomic Energy, but its academic work extends beyond nuclear power. IISc, established in 1909, conducts research and higher education. The IISERs combine science teaching with research training under the higher-education system.

Scientific knowledge and national needs

Basic science seeks explanations that can support many future applications. For instance, understanding the properties of materials can eventually improve industrial processes, energy technologies or medical instruments. The time between a discovery and its practical use may be long, which is one reason public support for fundamental science remains important.

Prelims focus

  • DST was established in May 1971.
  • CSIR was established in 1942.
  • CSIR-NPL, New Delhi: national metrology and measurement standards.
  • CSIR-CSMCRI, Bhavnagar: salt and marine-chemical research.
  • TIFR, Mumbai: fundamental research; established in 1945.
  • IISc, Bengaluru: scientific education and research; established in 1909.
  • Trap: A CSIR institute located in Gujarat remains part of a national research network.

[Department of Science and Technology, About DST; Council of Scientific and Industrial Research, About CSIR; CSIR-National Physical Laboratory, Vision and Mission; CSIR-Central Salt and Marine Chemicals Research Institute, About Us, section Genesis of CSMCRI; Bhabha Atomic Research Centre, About Us, section on the foundation of TIFR; Indian Institute of Science, History; sources consulted 2 November 2026.]

pictures.alt: Basic and applied research, researcher training and dependable measurement standards support the production of an industrial component.
pictures.caption: Scientific institutions contribute through different but connected functions.

title: Basic Science, Industrial Research and National Scientific Institutions

body:
Purpose of India's space programme

India's space programme develops scientific and technological capabilities for space exploration and practical national applications. Satellites support communication, weather observation, navigation, resource monitoring and disaster-related information. Launch vehicles carry satellites and other payloads into space.

The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is India's principal space research and development organisation. It was established on 15 August 1969, succeeding the Indian National Committee for Space Research (INCOSPAR), which had been formed in 1962. The Department of Space (DoS) was established in 1972, and ISRO came under it.

The Department of Space is the government department responsible for the national space programme. ISRO is a major organisation through which the department carries out research, development and space missions.

Main functions of ISRO

  • Developing launch vehicles and associated space technologies.
  • Designing and developing satellites for communication, navigation, observation and scientific purposes.
  • Conducting lunar, planetary and other scientific space missions.
  • Developing and applying satellite-based technologies to national needs.
  • Supporting space science, scientific data and education.

A communication satellite, for example, can relay information over large distances. An Earth-observation satellite gathers information about the Earth's surface and atmosphere. These are different applications even though both use satellites.

Important space centres and their mandates

CentreLocationMain responsibility
Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC)ThiruvananthapuramLaunch-vehicle technology.
U R Rao Satellite Centre (URSC)BengaluruSatellite design and development.
Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC SHAR)SriharikotaIntegration and launching of satellites and launch vehicles.
Space Applications Centre (SAC)AhmedabadSatellite payloads, sensors and applications.
National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC)HyderabadReception, processing and dissemination of remote-sensing data.

IN-SPACe and private participation

Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) is an autonomous, single-window agency under the Department of Space. It was formed following reforms intended to facilitate greater participation by non-governmental entities in space activities.

IN-SPACe promotes, enables, authorises and supervises relevant space activities undertaken by non-governmental entities. Its functions include facilitating access to suitable space infrastructure and coordinating with ISRO where required.

IN-SPACe headquarters is in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. This makes it especially important for Gujarat-related institution and location questions.

NSIL and commercial activities

NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) was incorporated on 6 March 2019. It is a Government of India company under the Department of Space and serves as the commercial arm of ISRO.

Its responsibilities include supporting industry participation in space-related production and marketing services and technologies arising from the space programme. Its commercial role is different from ISRO's principal research-and-development role and IN-SPACe's authorisation and facilitation role.

Physical Research Laboratory: Gujarat's basic space-science institution

The Physical Research Laboratory (PRL) was founded by Vikram Sarabhai in 1947 and formally established in Ahmedabad on 11 November 1947. It began with research on cosmic rays and the upper atmosphere and later expanded into other areas of physical and space sciences.

PRL operates under the Department of Space. It is a research institution, not India's satellite launch centre. The distinction matters because Sriharikota is associated with launches, while Ahmedabad is associated with SAC, PRL and IN-SPACe.

Prelims focus

  • ISRO: 15 August 1969.
  • Department of Space: 1972.
  • SDSC SHAR: Sriharikota; VSSC: Thiruvananthapuram.
  • SAC and IN-SPACe headquarters: Ahmedabad.
  • NSIL: incorporated 6 March 2019; commercial arm of ISRO.
  • PRL: founded by Vikram Sarabhai in Ahmedabad in 1947.
  • Trap: ISRO develops space technologies; IN-SPACe facilitates and authorises non-governmental activities; NSIL handles commercial responsibilities.

[Indian Space Research Organisation, About ISRO, sections Profile and ISRO Centres; ISRO, Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre; ISRO, NewSpace India Limited; Physical Research Laboratory, History, entries for 1947; sources consulted 2 November 2026.]

pictures.caption: Space research depends on specialised teams working on satellites and instruments.

body:
Why does defence require specialised research?

Defence forces require technologies suited to national security needs. These include equipment for detecting threats, secure communication, surveillance, protection, mobility and other military functions. Scientific and technological self-reliance helps a country develop and maintain capabilities appropriate to its requirements.

The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) is India's principal defence research and development organisation under the Ministry of Defence. It was formed in 1958 through the combination of existing defence research and technical development establishments.

Mandate of DRDO

DRDO undertakes research and development of technologies and systems intended to meet the needs of India's armed forces. It works across multiple scientific and engineering disciplines.

Major areas include:

  • Aeronautics: Research supporting military aviation technologies.
  • Electronics and sensors: Technologies used in detection, communication and surveillance.
  • Missiles and associated systems: Defence-related guided systems and supporting technologies.
  • Materials and protection: Research into materials and protective systems needed for defence applications.
  • Naval technologies: Research for maritime defence requirements.
  • Life sciences: Research relating to the health, protection and performance of personnel under demanding conditions.

Examples associated with DRDO's development activities include the Agni and Prithvi missile series, the Akash air-defence system, radar technologies and several other defence systems. These names illustrate the organisation's broad technological role; they do not mean that every component is manufactured by DRDO itself.

Research, production and operational use

Three functions should be distinguished:

  • Research and development: Scientists and engineers investigate requirements and develop or improve technologies.
  • Production: Appropriate manufacturing organisations and industries produce equipment and systems.
  • Operational use: The armed forces employ equipment in accordance with their service requirements.

These stages involve cooperation. A research organisation can help create a technology without being the organisation that ultimately manufactures, purchases or operates it.

DRDO and ISRO: an important distinction

DRDO and ISRO both employ advanced science and engineering, but their primary mandates differ. DRDO develops technologies for defence and national security. ISRO carries out India's space research, development and missions, including civil applications.

Some scientific techniques, materials or electronic components may have both civilian and defence uses. This overlap is called dual-use technology. The possibility of overlapping technologies does not remove the institutional distinction between DRDO and ISRO.

Prelims focus

  • DRDO was formed in 1958.
  • DRDO functions under the Ministry of Defence.
  • Its principal mandate is defence research, development and technological self-reliance.
  • Missiles, radars, aeronautics and defence-related life sciences are among its research areas.
  • ISRO was formed in 1969 and works under the Department of Space.
  • Trap: Defence research, industrial manufacturing and military operation are separate functions.

[Defence Research and Development Organisation, Ministry of Defence, Organisation, sections on History and Research Areas; DRDO, Frequently Asked Questions, When Was DRDO Formed?; Indian Space Research Organisation, About ISRO, Profile; sources consulted 2 November 2026.]

pictures.alt: Armed forces identify requirements, DRDO develops technology, industries produce systems, and armed forces use them; DRDO was formed in 1958.
pictures.caption: Defence technology moves from a research requirement to practical use through several organisations.
